summary: Independent curl/HTTP verification of Codex Review Gate 01 (CRG01-1 cross-tenant unit-type isolation + CRG01-2 production-event idempotency) against a live FastAPI + real Postgres backend. All 9 tests pass. Both invariants fully verified: cross-tenant leak is closed (spoofed organization_id filter is silently stripped, outsider sees only is_system=true entries) and per-batch idempotency behaves correctly for replay (200 + X-Idempotent-Replay: true), payload conflict (409 + detail.code=idempotency_key_payload_conflict), missing header (independent 201s), cross-batch key reuse (both 201, distinct rows), stocking transition (no double-transition on replay), high-concurrency race (6 parallel POSTs -> 1x201 + 5x200, exactly one DB row), and event/transition happy-path atomicity (PLANNED->STOCKED + event both persisted).

minor.issue: Enum mismatch between alembic and SQLAlchemy model: migration creates role_scope enum with lowercase labels ('platform','organization','farm') but the SQLAlchemy Enum(RoleScope, name='role_scope') column defaults to writing enum NAMES ('PLATFORM','ORGANIZATION','FARM'). Fresh test DB seeded via `alembic upgrade head` + `python -m app.seed` fails with `invalid input value for enum role_scope: "PLATFORM"`. The pytest suite works because conftest uses Base.metadata.create_all (which regenerates the enum with SQLAlchemy names). This is latent and will break `alembic upgrade head` + seed on any fresh staging/prod deploy. Recommended fix: add `values_callable=lambda e: [m.value for m in e]` to the Enum() column (or migrate labels to uppercase). Not part of CRG01 scope but worth flagging.

action_items: OPTIONAL/OUT-OF-SCOPE: fix role_scope enum name/value mismatch between alembic 0002 migration and SQLAlchemy model so `alembic upgrade head` + `python -m app.seed` works against a fresh Postgres DB (the CRG01 fixes themselves are correct and complete).
critical_code_review_comments: CRG01-1 fix in ProductionUnitTypeRepository.list_visible correctly ignores organization_id filter when the caller is not a member of that org (silent strip, no 403 leak signal). Verified.

CRG01-2 idempotency implementation is well-layered: (1) pre-insert lookup via (batch_id, idempotency_key), (2) SAVEPOINT-wrapped INSERT so IntegrityError from the partial unique index only rolls back the statement, (3) post-collision second lookup for the race winner. Payload hash covers event_type + validated data + is_final. Correct.

Partial unique index `uq_events_batch_idempotency_key ON production_events (batch_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL` is present and enforcing exactly-once at the DB layer. Verified.

Event/transition atomicity: transition and event share the request-scoped SQLAlchemy session; a raise from batch_service.transition propagates through the request handler, and the DB dep rolls back both writes. Happy path verified via curl.

Latent bug: role_scope enum labels differ between alembic (lowercase) and SQLAlchemy Enum column (writes NAMES = uppercase). Breaks a fresh `alembic upgrade head` + seed. Same issue would apply to any other native Postgres enum that goes through both paths. See minor issue above.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bug found in the CRG01-1 or CRG01-2 remediations. Both invariants hold against a real Postgres backend under both single-request and concurrent (6-way parallel) traffic. The only latent issue observed is unrelated to CRG01: the role_scope enum name/value mismatch between alembic and the SQLAlchemy model, which prevents `alembic upgrade head` + `app.seed` from succeeding on a fresh Postgres DB (workaround: use Base.metadata.create_all as the test fixtures do).
